name: Haruspex Null

stars.name: Haruspex
stars.notes: Millisecond pulsar whose rotation-beamed sweeps once lit the skies of the empire that worshipped it; radiation sterilizes every world in the system.

planets.name: Vitella
planets.notes: Glassy slag world fused by the ancient supernova; its surface still holds vitrified ripples like poured tallow.

planets.name: Extispex
planets.notes: Airless rock honeycombed with imperial divination vaults; sealed shafts descend toward the core where pulse-recordings were kept.

planets.name: Tarpeia
planets.notes: Radiation-blasted ice shell; beneath it, dead aqueduct machinery shows the empire once drew water here by remote artifice.

anomalies.name: The Answering Pulse
anomalies.notes: The pulsar's timing drifts measurably after strong broadcasts are aimed at it; cryptographers insist the intervals encode responses, though none agree on translations.

anomalies.name: Liver of the Sky
anomalies.notes: Dense clumps of supernova-forged matter warp trajectories without any visible body; pilots who survive call the safe channels 'the veins'.

asteroid_belts.name: Omen Fields
asteroid_belts.notes: Transuranic-rich debris entangled with the mascon shoals; drone mining is viable but every recovered ingot must be decontaminated of pulse-echo resonance.

stations.name: Capitoline Relay
stations.notes: Vestige Warden citadel-relay where sanctioned questions are transmitted toward Haruspex; its cipher vaults are rumored to hold eleven confirmed answers.

faction_control.notes: An ascetic order guarding both the ruins and the Pulse; access requires rites, escorts, and a question deemed worthy.

history: Old imperial charts record Haruspex's supernova as a sky omen heralding the empire's founding — and its collapse fell within a lifetime of the first decoded pulse.
Salvagers rediscovered Extispex's vaults two centuries ago; most died of radiation greed before the Wardens consolidated control.
Naval intelligence services quietly lease listening time at Capitoline Relay despite the Wardens' rules, convinced the Pulse answers whoever asks correctly.
description: Haruspex Null is a graveyard lit in strobes: a millisecond neutron star sweeping blue-white beams across three dead worlds. Vitrified Vitella, the vault-riddled rock Extispex, and frozen Tarpeia orbit through radiation that has kept the system sterile since the empire that built here burned with its own sun.

Light traffic approaches only under Warden escort, bound for Capitoline Relay or the drone lines working the Omen Fields. The Wardens permit no settlement, only vigil: they maintain the vaults of a forgotten empire whose people read the future in the Pulse's intervals, and their own cryptographers continue the practice under strict vows.

The critical question is whether the Pulse truly answers. Eleven transmissions are said to have received structured replies, each one verified accurate after the fact and each one describing something terrible. Visitors are welcome to broadcast a question of their own. The Wardens will not stop you. They will simply ask you to remain for the answer.
